Another Fraudulent Charge Complaint. I’m another person who had the rug pulled out from under them with their billing practices. I signed up for a 14-Day free trial and about three days in found it wasn’t for me. Upon sign up, you’re told that you’ll receive a reminder email before your trial is up that you’ll be moved to a paid subscription. The day before my trial ended, they took the money and THEN emailed me and said my trial was up the following day. I wrote support and asked for my money back for the reasons I detailed here. They responded six days later telling me my subscription was cancelled (which I had already done at this point) and that I won’t be charged anymore. I responded and thanked them for that and inquired about the refund and no response. This was going on three weeks ago. I encourage folks who have had a similar experience to let the Better Business Bureau, the FTC, and econsumer dot gov know. No matter the efficacy of an app like this, taking money from people actively trying to improve their capacity for executive function is incredibly sinister. It’s preying on the very thing people using this app are seeking help with.
